reviews.text:
The atmosphere here is great, with lots of seating on the second and third floors and plenty of power outlets. I had two pastries (a bit too sweet, but tasty) and a black coffee, which was decent.

However, I’m only giving this place 2 stars. There’s no Wi-Fi — the city’s public network wasn’t working — and prices are higher than nearby cafes. Most off-putting, though, is the number of directive signs posted everywhere. While individually reasonable, they create a slightly stressful vibe when all you want is to enjoy a coffee in peace.

The atmosphere is really nice. There are plenty of seats on the 2nd and 3rd floors and many power outlets, making it convenient to work. I had two pastries (a little sweet but delicious) and an Americano, which was okay.

However, I only give it 2 stars. There was no wifi, and the public wifi provided by the city did not work. The prices are a bit expensive compared to nearby cafes.

What was most disappointing was the information posted everywhere. “No smoking”, “Do not open the window”, “The restroom is for customers only”, “Order one drink per person”, “Use the microwave one at a time”, etc… Each is understandable, but there are so many that it feels overwhelming when I want to relax at a cafe.

Because this bread is made by a world-class baker, it is different from the basics.
Yakisoba bread, egg tarts, and red bean bread were all satisfying!

reviews.text: The bread is varied and delicious, but they seem to be paying too much attention to the lack of space. There are many similar coffee shops nearby, so if it takes a while, it's convenient without worrying about other places.

reviews.author: Ashley Jang
reviews.text:
It’s a very hip, hanok-style cafe. The interior with the concept of a furnace is very impressive here and there, and the traditional version of the Kedheun song is also played, and I really like the comfortable yet unique atmosphere, as if I'm in a completely different world from the forest of buildings outside.
There were a lot of customers because it was the weekend, but the tables were spaced out comfortably and the ceiling was high so it wasn't stuffy and the atmosphere was calm.
The variety of bread on the bread display is truly enormous. Not only do they have everything from traditional breads such as red bean and black sesame to chocolate base, baked cookies, focaccia, etc., but there are also many breads with unique concepts that are difficult to find elsewhere.
The traditional tea I tried for the first time in a while was delicious, and the staff was very friendly, so I felt good during my stay♡
It's a space you'll want to visit again and again with precious guests.

reviews.author: Philosophizing
reviews.text: Agung, a newly opened bakery near Jonggak Station!! This is a place where you can taste the very unique hat-shaped financier. The mugwort rice cake was also very chewy and good. A place I wanted to recommend to foreign tourists as well.

reviews.author: national_jiographic
reviews.text: This is a recently opened large cafe. It has a complete Hanok feel and is a large bakery cafe that is not common in this location, so it's nice to stay there. The coffee was very delicious, but I think I'll have to try the bread next time. The bread was cheaper than other bakery cafes.

reviews.author: B K
reviews.text:
I visited this place while passing by because it was unique.
It's a pretty spacious cafe.
It has a slightly Korean(?) bakery cafe feel, but the character has been brought to life quite well. I was disappointed that there was no makgeolli fermented bread because I went late in the day, but the other breads were also quite delicious.
The staff seemed friendly too.
A place that sells porridge and has many other things to eat.
Worth a visit at least once!

reviews.author: Taemi Lee
reviews.text:
This bakery cafe makes you feel like you're going back to the Joseon Dynasty and eating bread instead of rice cake.
There are many breads with Korean flavor added to them. They are even delicious.
It looks good too.
The interior is unique, and there is a furnace sculpture that looks like something out of a Korean history museum experience hall, as well as freshly shaped desserts.
I ate Duck Hanssam Focaccia and Apricot Fig Campagne.
It's seriously delicious. I need to stop by Jongno often.
Since it's a weekday, there aren't many people, but it seems to be very crowded on the weekend.
It's a good bakery cafe.

The best coffee restaurant.
It's been a long time since I've seen a place that makes coffee so well and with such love.
There seemed to be a lot of delicious desserts too. Every menu item is colorful and has an authentic feel.
It seemed like a lot of attention was paid to every detail throughout the cafe, and the interior felt cozy and comfortable.
Since it was in front of Euljiro Entrance Station, there seemed to be a lot of office workers, especially foreigners.
It was nice to visit alone as the interior was spacious and well-equipped.

reviews.author: tomato
reviews.text: First of all, it’s spacious and the bread is delicious.  In particular, the mugwort Mont Blanc Danish is delicious with red beans and cream inside. I went around 3 o'clock and there was almost no bread. The downside is that the chairs are wooden chairs without cushions. The coffee is not hot. I ordered mugwort blanc hot, but the injeolmi kimchi was cold, so it was vaguely warm, and the Americano wasn't hot either. If you like it hot, it might be a good idea to tell us in advance, just in case.

Since they are good at making sourdough, the pastry is delicious without being sticky.

reviews.author: BONG
reviews.text:
I remember it was originally a Quiznos or sandwich shop, but it seems to have recently changed to Baskin Robbins.

Baskin seems to be much more popular than sandwiches, and it is clearly visible from both directions, stimulating the appetite. Basically, you order at a kiosk, but since there is only one kiosk, it is inconvenient during crowded evenings. The employees' hands seemed to be quite quick, and there seemed to be a lot of group ice cream or cake orders using corporate cards.

Products related to the event are displayed in a huge display, and the seats in the store themselves are not that cramped.

There are quite a few foreigners and it is a bit uncomfortable to sit and eat comfortably for a long time as the interior is too clearly visible.

Still, I'm glad I ended up in a place where I thought it would be nice to have one around here.
